notes.title: Next Update Incoming!
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey everyone!

I wanted to stop by and say that the next HUGE update will be out by the end of the week. I'm doing some final touches and some bug testing to make sure everything runs smoothly, but this update is going to be THE LARGEST UPDATE TO LAWLESS LANDS YET!

Tons of new content including over 5 new side quests, expanded previous side quests, 2 new enemy factions, 9 new enemies and encounters, 1 new major settlement, many new exploration areas, reworked supply stash mechanics, the foraging system, 15 more soundtracks, and so much more!

Let me tell you a bit about my personal favorite new feature.

[u]The Foraging System[/u]

The foraging system is one that I've been putting off because I personally don't like it in games, but now that I have it all working, I gotta say that it's pretty awesome and definitely expands the game. Basically, there are 10 herbs in the game that are used for alchemy. Until now, the only ways to get them were to find them randomly (and rarely) off of dead enemies and by buying them. Now, you'll be able to find them randomly across all outdoor maps, and even some caves and dungeons!

They are randomly spawned with a pretty neat little system that I designed that takes several different factors into account when spawning them. Of course, it wouldn't work without graphics for each plant, so I made those too. It is not a required feature, and if nothing else, it adds some more vegetation and scenery, but to those who like crafting, it will make life significantly easier and also give another form of value to each area based on what types of plants they spawn. They will always be completely randomized, so they will never be in the same place.

Like I said, there are 10 different plant herbs that you can find. They are broken down into which type of terrain they are located such as swamps and near water, forests and wilds, fields and plains, hills and mountains, and underground.

Each (exterior) area can be up to 3 different types of the above terrains.

I'm not going to give away what spawns where, so you'll have to figure that out for yourselves, but it'll be worth it!

I'm looking forward to hear what everyone thinks!

notes.title: Lawless Lands - The Foolish Hero
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey everyone!

So, I had some people asking me if the early access launch trailer was an accurate reflection of the game in its current state. Simply: No.

The game has come a very long way over the past several months and that video was only showing the initial alpha stages of the game. I haven't had time to go back and make a new showcase video, but I did make a short gameplay video. When I do have time, I'll go back and update it and make a new trailer that better shows off the game in its current state. It's much more polished, fluid, and just better all around now. At that time, there was also a lot less content. Perhaps around 6-10 hours of gameplay.

Since then, the game has literally quadrupled in size. Before it's finished, it will continue to get larger and larger. There are hours upon hours of gameplay and various things to do in the game including side quests, the first chapter of the main quest, exploring, raiding dungeons, delving into the story rich conversations with NPCs, reading the lore, upgrading, seeing the randomized events, fighting dozens of different enemies and all the various factions, and so on.

I ended up dying (yes, even I die when I play my own game) while playing, but it sort of worked out for the best. It showed part of a quest that was added in one of the last few updates without spoiling the entire thing.

The next update is nearly ready and I'm just adding in some final touches, so it should be ready soon.

If you want to see the short gameplay video I made, check it out here: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1814900399

I was foolish and tried facing an enemy group of ghouls while I was alone and completely outnumbered. Foolish thing to do in Lawless Lands.

Don't forget that the game and DLCs for it are on sale now for a huge discount, so don't miss out!

notes.title: 6/7/19 Development Status Update - Randomized World Events
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey guys!

Just wanted to stop by with a little more information on the randomized world event system.

Over the past few days, I've been working, tweaking, improving, and expanding this system. It went from being a few simple, 1-time events, to somewhere around 200 different possibilities and a huge variety at that. Originally, I was aiming for just 10 different events that could take place. Simple but effective. I decided to expand many of them to have several different outcomes or occurrences to be even more diversified and unique. An example of this would be the "Decayed Remains" event. Long story short, you come upon several bodies that look as if they have been there for a long time. There are 15 different outcomes to this single event. You might find some valuable loot, wolves looking to feed, the bodies could start growling at you and stand up and start shambling towards you, it could be a trap, etc. There is so much variety. Wandering merchants and blacksmiths, lost cargo, shady vagabonds, bad omens, sudden weather changes, the list goes on.

I was very excited about this addition to the game as it put my storytelling skills to the test even more than the quests and will definitely make things more interesting, especially while traveling on the world map. I really feel that this steps the game up and pushes it further in the right direction for what I'm going for. A true-to-heart, old-fashioned RPG.

The main story is now 100% my absolute priority.

I'll have more info soon! The update will likely hit next week at some point.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

I wanted to stop by for a quick status update and let you all know how work on the game has been going for the past few days.

I've made a lot of progress on the main questline as well as redesigning the experience and fame earning system for the main questline.

I've also laid out the framework for the upcoming randomized world map events feature. This will include a variety of things but is separate from the randomized encounter system. You'll be able to experience more lore, roleplay opportunities, and a variety of other side events such as wandering merchants, small side activity opportunities, and more. This will now GUARANTEE that each adventure is unique. As if the randomized loot, encounters, weather, and other random events weren't enough, now there will be even more! It's not finished yet, but it will be soon!

I've added several new graphics to the game and added a lot more ambient decorations such as more torches with ambient lighting, more unique NPCs with unique lore, some new special effects, and more!

The character creation skin selection was already improved but was still missing something. Now, it is a lot more streamlined to use and should allow for much higher player comfort when using it.

There are a lot of other things to look forward to in the next update, but I don't want to give away all of the surprises.

[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey everyone!

I set my alarm for 8:15 AM this morning so I could get up and add one more side quest and some extra polish for this update and then set it live. Some might say I have a problem since I work on Sundays, especially so early in the morning, and I'd agree with them. :-)

So, the change log is pretty lengthy already, but the amount of actual changes, improvements, and additions to the game with this update is absolutely huge.

First, there are several new side quests that add lore, roleplay, and side content to the game. Second, the main city (Pyrshen) is almost completed now. It took a long time, but it's almost finished. This update added a load of new areas, buildings, sectors, and more to it. Third, manipulation in the form of persuasion and intimidation have been reworked so it is now a lot more like a true roleplaying game. Next, there are two new backgrounds (early game class archtype loadouts, but the game is not class-based) including the Alchemist for the Nobles and the Hexer for the commoners. notes.title: 3/14/19 Development Status Update
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey guys!

I wanted to stop by and leave a quick status update about the next content update. It will have a lot of new things, quality of life improvements, player comfort improvements, and as always, lots of content.

I'm starting to have a pretty good professional portfolio at this point, and I'm almost finished with college and expanding my toolkit skillset, getting my Bachelors Degree of Science in Game Programming and Development at SNHU. I have a lot of working knowledge and experience and skills with this stuff now, so if you've been following my games since I started, you can definitely see progress and improvements. With this comes more responsibility and capabilities.

I'm going to start making change logs look more professional instead of just clobbering everything in together. I had a bug section and a change section, but it will now be broken up into different areas for ease of viewing and accessing the data.

I'm also going to be going back and updating (as I have been) previous games of mine with improvements and player comfort changes but not altering the games anymore really at this point. My newer games will continue to feature new innovative mechanics, ideas, and features of their own.

I still love making games like Disgraced, Waste Walkers, and Lawless Lands because I enjoy the genre and enjoy building these style games. I plan to do more, but I'll also be expanding to newer engines and trying new things.

For those of you who followed my game, Affliction, you'll know how tirelessly I worked on that game, but the engine just couldn't keep up. It was not a good engine, but it appeared to be. I learned a lot from this experience and that's where I got a lot of my coding practice, but I'll definitely be more careful next time I leave my comfort zone and try out other possibilities.

As for the next update with LL, Stolts (Northern Barbarian Hordes) have been added to the game. Some new quests have been added, lots of improvements to combat, more balancing, and a lot of other various things. One of the largest changes is the new equip slot "Accessory". I know this isn't unique, but the manner in which it is used in this game is. It can hold a variety of things such as holy symbols, special scabbards for your weapons, armor upgrades like thicker padding, reinforced mail, and extra plating, braces, smaller bags now equip in that slot as well so you can carry even more loot. Coin purses have been remade so they automatically add their contents to your pockets instead of needing to be used first, and other various changes like this are also being worked on.

New skills have been added, a gambling system and custom game (A modified version of "Fray" from our game Disgraced) that allows more replayability and expands greatly on gameplay, and also many new locations.

I've read a lot of posts recently about how players crave old school style RPGs and that's what the goal is here, but I've seen a lot of people complaining about dynamic enemy leveling. Some players like this feature, but most do not. As such, I've GREATLY reduced the rate at which enemies improve. Down to like 1-2% per level on stats only. I think this will strike a good balance, as before it was roughly 7-11%.

The next update will be available soon, and as always, I'll continue to strive to make the best games possible. With all of your help and support, it is truly possible.

Thank you for reading, and thank you for your support.

-[b]Eric "Corrosion" Plasencia[/b] :CStudios:

[b]Lawless Lands,[/b]

[i]"Lawless Lands is meant to look, play, and feel like an old-school role-playing-game. Combined with modern features and favorites, this hybrid approach has been carefully calibrated to offer a unique and original experience of balance and flexibility, all while retaining the depth of a traditional RPG. The game features its own theme, lore, and storyline, and the player is placed at the center of it all. The systems in the game all coexist and collaborate to bring life and flavor to the game world. There are often many ways to complete an objective or to reach a goal. The equipment system is deep, and a handy prybar or a strong rope may become useful or even essential at times and could mean the difference between life and death. There is a lot of diversity between gear such as weapons and armor, and there are many different ways to build a character and shape them into a specific role, or even a jack-of-all-trades. Skills and talents also reflect this. The character creation system allows you to choose every aspect about your character. This includes gender, race, familial background, occupational background, traits, religion, alignment, appearance, skills, talents, and more. Create the fiercest slayer, the mightiest knight, the wisest wizard, the deadliest archer, the stealthiest assassin, or absolutely anything in between. The classless advancement system offers complete and total freedom without constraints. The game is intended to bridge the gap between traditional and modern styled RPGs."[/i]

The game still has a long way to go before completion, but as of right now, we feel it really gives the feelings and nostalgia of playing traditional RPGs. We will continue to improve the game and polish it and strive to bring you all the best game possible.

Thank you to everyone who has been so kind and helpful and for showing their support! We wouldn't be here without you guys.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: Be Part of Lawless Lands - LIMITED TIME OFFER
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey everyone!

=== [b]Introduction:[/b] ===

This announcement is mainly for fans of the game and people who would like the chance to appear in the game either by getting a custom skin for their own use or by appearing as an NPC. Or Both! Or create a quest of your very own!

Starting TODAY on the 7th of February, a special limited time offer and promotion is going to be done for the game. [u]This will run until the 7th of March[/u], so it is for one month.

=== [b]Details:[/b] ===

If you'd like to support the game further and appear in game, all you have to do is donate a minimum of $2.50 USD to our donation paypal account!

=== [b]Fine Details:[/b] ===

[b]Militia[/b] Donators who donate $2.50 or more USD will be able to submit a custom skin that [u]they have made[/u] and they will be able to play as it in the game and [u]get a boost of 50 gold lords[/u]!

[b]Guard[/b] Donators who donate $5.00 or more will have [u]a skin made for them[/u] (as they describe) and will be able to play as them in game and [u]get a boost of 100 gold lords[/u]!

[b]Soldier[/b] Donators who donate $10.00 USD or more will be able to [u]create their own NPC to be seen by everyone in thegame[/u]. Tell us who you want them to be, what you want them to say, and anything else you can think of! They also [u]get a boost of 200 gold lords[/u]!

[b]Captain[/b] Donators who donate $20.00 USD or more will be able to [u]write a side quest to appear in the game[/u] and be played by everyone! This can be pretty much anything as long as it fits into the theme of the game - medieval, low fantasy. They also [u]get a boost of 400 gold lords[/u]!

=== [b]How it Works:[/b] ===

Interested players and community members can make their donations here:
https://www.paypal.com/donate/?token=l5PaVf3Ds_APMjxdEENCD-4Nrq4U2ra1OtA0jxi_QVQLgjAfahMpNQcrT02kT3vExB4n5G&country.x=US&locale.x=US

When you make a donation, send an email to: crsvstudiosspprt@gmail.com and let us know that you sent in a donation. We'll confirm with you within 2 business days. Depending on the amount you donated, we'll go from there.

*For people donating to get their skin in game, they'll need to give us a name of 16 characters or less that they can type in for their name when they make their character and that will be used to activate their skin and grant them their bonus gold lords.*

So, to sum it all up in some quick and easy steps:

1-Decide if you want to donate or not

2-Decide on how much you want to donate (please see the ranks above)

3-Donate to https://www.paypal.com/donate/?token=l5PaVf3Ds_APMjxdEENCD-4Nrq4U2ra1OtA0jxi_QVQLgjAfahMpNQcrT02kT3vExB4n5G&country.x=US&locale.x=US

4-Send an email to crsvstudiosspprt@gmail.com and tell us who you are and how much you donated so that we can confirm

5-We'll get back to you within 2 business days and start figuring out how to get your content in the game

6-Your content will be added and you'll be able to access it in the next update

[u]Remember, this offer starts TODAY on the 7th of February and ends on the 7th of March, one month from tomorrow[/u].

If you have any questions or concerns, please feel free to post here or send an email to: crsvstudiosspprt@gmail.com

See you soon!

***PLEASE NOTE: If you are already a donator or VIP, you do not need to donate here in order to benefit from these rewards. Just message me personally.***

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

"The Supporter Pack DLC is for people who'd like to show their continued support for us at Corrosive Studios and to help us continue to grow and do what we do while also giving you an edge in the game by rewarding your character with some unique tools to aid them in their travels. Exclusives:

-Strange Shield - It may not be much to look at, but it will never leave you empty-handed. It is completely unbreakable and it will last longer than any who bear it.
-Ring of Tranquility - A magic ring that can both cure and calm a targeted ally, but it cannot be used in combat and it leaves the target in a tranquil state.
-Pitcher of Plenty - An enchanted pitcher of water that slowly refills over time. Larger than a typical waterskin, this pitcher will quench even the worst of thirst and refresh your company so they're ready for whatever adventure you choose to embark on!
-Lucky Lord Coin - Ever find yourself in a situation where you don't know which choice to make or which way to go? Worry no more! The Lucky Lord Coin can be used to help you out! Extras: 
-1x Tome - A textbook written by a scholar of great knowledge. Use this on any character of your choice for them to instantly gain 100 experience!
-1x Orb - A powerful magic orb that can revive the dead. Use this in combat to revive any ally with 20% vigor!"

notes.title: 12/7/18 Development Status Update
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey everyone!

Just wanted to stop by and post a quick status update. The next update will feature several player comfort adjustments and changes. One of the largest changes is in regards to combat and damage, but this is by no means the only change!

In our previous game, [i]Disgraced[/i], there was a random number from 0 to 4 being added to every successful hit. In [i]Lawless Lands[/i], this changed to a base of 1 damage to make sure at least 1 damage was always added. This will no longer be the case.

I've made a change to the damage calculation to add a random number from 0 to 3 to be added to all successful hits. If 0 is added and the armor rating outweighs damage, the attack is blocked and no damage is taken! This will add some new methods and tactics to combat. It also makes battles a little more stressful because everyone can do up to 3x the base damage that they were previously able to. 

This does not mean that the combatants in the game become glass cannons like in [i]Disgraced[/i], but it does mean that you'll have to be more careful and even the best armor may not save your life anymore.

Other changes include updates to some of the skills, readability changes, and various other tweaks.

Some new weapons have been added including a boomerang, bolas, a truncheon, and some weapons have been updated with new stats and icons. The kukri icon now actually shows a kukri, too.

Vulkold is also under construction. 

The enemy scaling has also been adjusted to give the enemies a little more advancement points towards the higher levels. Specifically after level 10 or so is when they'll really start putting up more of a fight, but for now, the game is much more balanced and the player is not such a tank. 

I was testing this all day today and before the change, I would get the heaviest medim armor, a broad sword, and a targe shield, and I'd absolutely wreck anything in my way. Including groups of up to 5-6 enemies.

After the change, as a melee tank, I was able to take down 2/7 enemies alone before I was destroyed. This is how it should be. Manage your team and your equipment choices wisely.

That's all for now!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: 11/17/18 Development Status Update
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey everyone!

I know it's been a bit since my last post, life's been crazy lately and one of my computers needed to have some work done on it and I still haven't gotten it back as of yet.

Work has still continued over the past few weeks, though, and a lot of changes, improvements, and new content will be available for the next update, which I plan to release this week around the holiday!

A new companion, updated graphics for several characters, new icon artwork for several items, new gear and equipment choices, more crafting recipes, new items and consumables, a new side quest, the finalization of the town of Mirone, new enemies, and much more! The resource system also had some more work done to it as well, so that is also something to look forward to!

A minor but important change has also been done to the supply system. Instead of ticking down at 1 point every so often, it will now tick at whatever your current active company size is. So, if you have 2 companions, it will go down at 3 points per tick. That means you'll need to start feeding your company! Don't worry, as it doesn't drastically change the game play, and there isn't much of a change in how to manage your company, most of the time, food was a good way to increase Spirit and Vigor when out of combat on injured company members. Just take in mind that the food system is slightly more important now. Some prices and statistics have been slightly altered to account for this change and to keep with the overall balance. You can still always use those wells and refill your water skins to avoid unnecessary costs and fish at fishing spots as well.

The Steam avatars for the group have been updated so you can see some of the graphical improvements on some of the characters already!

I'll have more info within the next few days!

Until then, journey safe in the [i]Lawless Lands[/i].

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: 10/26/18 Development Status Update
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hello, adventurers!

So, many of you saw that last week, I made a post about having to focus on school last week and not being able to work on the game due to my finals. Well, my finals are done and I got A's in all my classes this semester and A's on all of my finals! :-) I'm proud to be able to say that!

This week, I worked on the game again and added the bandit faction which currently has 5 different variants.

I also added a new feature and skill to the game - whenever you rest on the world map using adventuring gear, you have a 5% chance that when you wake, your horse will be gone. Either loose or stolen, somehow that pesky horse got away. The skill - Horse Master - prevents this from ever happening.

I also worked on the main storyline a bit, and added the first quest for it. I worked some more on the world map, added random dialogues for the corpses littered everywhere, added some new NPCs, and made the Northern road of Pyrshen.

A few new items have been added to the game as well. The executioner's hood is probably going to be the most popular, as it adds bonus chance to cause panic.

There was a lot of other background stuff done too, such as removing some music tracks that didn't fit the theme well and the addition of a few others.

Stay tuned! The next update will likely come out next week!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: 9/28/18 Development Status Update
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey guys!

I wanted to stop by and let everyone know what got accomplished on the game today.

First, I added some new enemies. I introduced the "zombie" line of enemies including the Ghoul and the Wretch. The Ghoul is very similar to a zombie in almost every aspect except they aren't really undead. They are more like horribly diseased, insane victims of the plague. They have darkened skin, and emit terrible odors. The Wretch is a weaker, but slightly faster version of the Ghoul and is pale grey. I also added a decrepit skeleton to the skeletal army line of enemies. He is missing an arm, has a hole in his head, and his only way to defend himself is an old wooden shield. His primary tactic is to block, but he may bash you with his shield from time to time.

Second, I did bug fixes and improvements to polish the game some more. I added some new hints to help with confusing or difficult tasks as well.

Third, AceHangman, a truly helpful and dedicated friend created a village to put into the game and I spent the afternoon converting it. It's called Durgim's Mill and contains several areas to explore and visit.

More development status updates will come in the future, so stay tuned! The next update will be out in about a week!

notes.title: 9/23/18 Development Status Update
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey guys!

So, I know I haven't made a status post in a few days. I've been extremely busy and have had a lot of stuff going on, but I have still been working and brainstorming for the game.

The biggest thing coming in the next update so far is changes to the advancement system and character creation. Instead of starting with a character who is pretty bland and then slowly building them up (in terms of attributes - called aspects in the game), characters will start off much more defined. All aspects now start at 2 instead of 1 and players will be given 4 points to spend across the 4 attributes during character creation. Characters will no longer be given attribute points when they level up, and instead, will only get mastery (skill) points. In order to increase attributes, you'll need to use magic items and equipment, and I am coming up with other ways to do this such as the resource system or crafting system. I decided to make these changes to  improve diversity among characters and to also have characters be naturally stronger. All enemies have also been adjusted accordingly.

The next change is the addition of character birth places. You can now choose where your character was born in the realm. There are 4 choices. Crossia - +1 physique, Stothlheim/Langmord - +1 power, Sagerov - +1 posture, and Guilanal - +1 prowess. Crossians are a feudalistic and defensive people, and they gain bonus protection from this. Northerners from Stothlheim - Stolts - and their kin from the West lands of Langmord - Langmordish - are warmongers and conquerors. They are bred for battle, and benefit from bonus aggression. The Sagerovians come from the marshlands and forests of Sagerov and are masters of survival in harsh terrain. They benefit from bonus resistance and knowledge of the weaknesses of their foes. Lastly, the Guilaners from the South dunes of Guilanal, are nomadic masters of the desert lands. They benefit from bonus reaction speed.

All companions have been given their backgrounds and have been updated with the new stat system. They will all now be more distinct and have even more of a unique play style. The tutorial has also been updated with the new changes so it is accurate and up to date.

Work will continue on the next update and much more will be added before it is released, but I'll continue making announcements every so often, explaining changes and improvments.

Stay tuned! The update will be out as soon as possible.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: 9/16/18 Development Status Update
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey everyone!

So, at the moment of writing this, I'm falling asleep at the keyboard. I've been working for three days straight on schoolwork and on the game. As you can imagine, it's pretty exhausting.

It is good news, though. I've gotten a lot done over the past few days. 

I added a new companion to the game, Kezyrek the Raider. He's from the Northlands and he has a pretty unique build. Poison items and crafting have also been added to the game so this adds some new strategies for combat. A new equipment slot for shoulders is now available for all characters. I added this because some wearable equipment overlapped each other and that caused some issues and wasn't realistic and lowered customization. A new settlement, Stilbel, has also been added and is ready for exploring. New holy symbols have been added to the game and they give different benefits, as well. There are now three versions including: wooden, silver, and gold. A wearable harness has been added to allow more carrying capacity, too. A new line of enemies also comes into the game for the next update. The Plagued Rabble. There are five variants including the regular Plagued Rabble, Spearman, Clubman, Axeman, and Daggerman. With all the stuff listed above, numerous bugs and other problems have been fixed.

Another thing that I did was type up a large document for the lore of the game and it contains the background story as well briefings on the different situations going on. This will be part of the Heroic Edition DLC when it is released. It's not needed to enjoy the game, but it can certainly give players some valuable information on the game world.

The update should be ready in another day ot two, so stay tuned!

notes.title: 9/7/18 Development Status Update
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Hey everyone!

So, we're just about 2 days away from release and I wanted to give another quick status update over what I got accomplished today.

For the most part, today was about polishing what's currently available. I did things like making sure the skeletons were immune to bleeding, and that the quests that are in game were bug free. I didn't notice from several playtests, but there were a few hidden issues that I got solved today and I can confidently say that it is now a fluid experience.

I added some new skills to the game today for both the player characters and even enemies. Things like lick wound for wolves, bone setting for skeletons, and a few tricks for the player to use to help in combat. I created a lot more sprites for the game today, too. Now, there's no longer just militia protecting Crossia. There's now actual watchmen and even watch captains.

I also added over 20 new items and equipment. A camouflage cloak, capes, a carrying coat, magic rings, a utility belt, prybars, and many more. It's really starting to take form and have a very real role playing feel to it.

The two currently available followers - Corban and Tarawyn - are pretty useful and can compliment a variety of builds. I won't give away exactly who or what they are, everyone can find that out for themselves on September 10th.

I plan to add bandits and highwaymen in the near future and also plague victims as the next enemy types to be implemented into the game.

I'd really like to add usable lore items into the game that will award experience to the main character when they are used. Sometime in the future. Things like personal diaries, journals, important documents, and the like. I think that these items will really bring the game to life and give it more depth. Being able to immerse players in the game's atmosphere is something I'm trying to focus on so it is a "full" experience.

Of course, there will also be achievements in the game that you can earn to show off on Steam. Right now, with their new systems in place, Steam is only allowing me to have up to 100 achievements but I think that's doable. Even if the game is going to be gigantic. Once I start selling enough copies and Steam "learns" about my product, hopefully, the cap will be removed and I'll be able to add a whole bunch for all the different quests and activities to partake in. My previous RPG games always had just around 100 achievements, but this one is supposed to be much larger.

There is still a very long way to go for [i]LL[/i], but it is already pretty solid, if I do say so myself. Overall, I think the game, so far, is a really good start, and a good foundation to build upon and make a really fun product.

I appreciate any and all help and support. Believe me, doing this alone is not easy. It means a lot when I get feedback and hear about you guys playing and enjoying my work. That's honestly the best.

Thanks for reading, everyone. I hope you're all as excited as I am for release!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: Lawless Lands 9/2/18 Status Update
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Today, I was able to get a lot accomplished and finish up several things on my to do list for the game.

With help from my friend Acehangman, I was able to add skeletal enemies to the game. There are currently 5 variants including a skeletal clubman, archer, swordsman, spearman, and maceman. Beware the armies of the dead! 

Another thing I was able to finish up today was the religion system. There are three main religious deities in which you can follow. Ashentarra, the goddess of Justice, peace, and charity is the first. Second, Sielias. The god of free will, balance, and dreams. Lastly, Vekran. The god of secrets, mischief, and shadows. You can also choose to be atheist or to not follow one specific figure. Each of the deities will give you a specific unique blessing whenever you pray to them at a shrine by using a candle. There is a chance that your prayers will be answered or ignored. A devoted religious character has a higher chance than one who does not follow a specific figure. The blessings give status effects and bonuses to the player's character and can greatly aid in a variety of ways.

Another full length quest from one of my personal D&D sessions was also added today. It counts as a side quest but it has its own unique storyline to it. It's not a huge quest but it is certainly interesting and should add some depth to the game world. 

I also added some more equipment and items to the game today and greatly polished several areas and features. 

There is a lot more than I plan to do over the next few days before release so stay tuned for more status updates.

That's all for now!

notes.title: Quick Announcement Regarding Release
notes.content:
[b]Lawless Lands[/b],

Due to some unexpected delays regarding the Steam build for the game and the setup on Steam itself, I've had to push back the release date for [i]LL[/i] by three (3) days. [u]The new release date is September 10[/u]. This will give me more time to add more content for the first release, so it's not a complete loss. I'm hoping the few day push will be worth it in the long run, as it will be a little closer to completion than without those additional few days.

I sincerely apologize for the delay and any inconvenience or disappointment this may cause. 

The current state of the game is pretty solid. There are a lot of lore and background dialogues, descriptions, and texts in the game. There are a handful of side quests and they are all pretty unique and there are several side activities to do as well. The main story is a huge work in progress and so is the world map, but many features are fully finished (though more content will be added to them) such as character creation, skills, spells, abilities, traits, and that kind of stuff. Weapons, armor, equipment, and items are pretty much done but they aren't all yet available to get in the game. They are already in the game though, just not obtainable yet. There are 3 settlements which can be visited so far including the hamlets of Ostrem and Hawbrun and the village of Thumel. Not to mention the places inside each settlement. There are a few locations to explore, and a few other places to visit and see. Each has its own unique flavor and personality. Dozens more will be added by the time the game is fully released, obviously. There are a few enemy races to fight including cave weavers (spiders), wolves, 9 different orc variations including berserkers, hunters, and butchers. Some features in the game are pretty bare bone right now and need to be fully implemented such as crafting, the resource system, and other smaller features.

I believe the game has a good development journey ahead and is shaping up really nicely already.

Thanks for reading!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:
